raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

With `use_remove_padding`, the FSDP engine packs a micro-batch into one `(1, total_nnz)` row and passes only `position_ids` to the model. transformers then re-derives `cu_seqlens` / `max_seqlen` from `position_ids` inside **every attention layer** (`nonzero`, `.item()`, a Python bool on a tensor in `_is_packed_sequence`), and flash-attn converts the tensor `max_seqlen` to an int. Each of these is a host-device sync, and they repeat in the activation-checkpoint recompute and in the backward.

For Qwen2.5-0.5B SFT (24 layers, 8 micro-batches per step) this is about **2,400 `cudaStreamSynchronize` calls per step**, and the GPU is idle for ~16–25% of the step while the host waits. verl's own `monkey_patch.py` carries a TODO about passing these boundaries explicitly.

The engine already knows the boundaries (the nested-tensor offsets). This PR passes them as `cu_seq_lens_q/k` (int32) and `max_length_q/k` (Python ints), the `FlashAttentionKwargs` transformers accepts for this. It costs one sync per micro-batch: syncs drop from ~2,400 to 85 per step and GPU busy time rises to ~93%.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Related but not overlapping:
  - #7137 (open) passes explicit `cu_seqlens` in the Ulysses SP patch, mainly to fix an mRoPE crash. This PR deliberately leaves SP > 1 unchanged, so the two are complementary; once both land, the SP gate here could be lifted.
  - #8300 (shared-prefix packing) and #7932 (critic boundary detection) touch nearby lines in `transformer_impl.py` but solve different problems.
  - No open or closed PR passes the packed boundaries to flash attention on the unsharded FSDP path.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

A/B on one RTX 5090, torch 2.8.0+cu128, flash-attn 2.8.3, transformers 5.16.1, GSM8K SFT batches through the engine's own `train_batch` / `infer_batch` (the calls the RL actor/critic workers make). Baseline is a worktree of main; 2 interleaved repeats × 10 measured batches (n=20) per cell; each run starts only when the GPU is idle and CPU load is low.

| config | path | main (s/step) | this PR (s/step) | time saved |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-0.5B, 2k tokens/micro-batch | train / log-prob | 4.154 / 1.168 | 3.456 / 1.038 | 16.8% / 11.1% |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B, 8k (SFT default) | train / log-prob | 1.973 / 0.568 | 1.778 / 0.518 | 9.8% / 8.9% |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B, 16k | train / log-prob | 1.683 / 0.486 | 1.615 / 0.461 | 4.0% / 5.2% |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B, FSDP2, 8k | train / log-prob | 2.098 / 0.585 | 1.827 / 0.544 | 12.9% / 7.1% |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B, fused kernels, 8k | train / log-prob | 2.875 / 0.921 | 2.655 / 0.874 | 7.7% / 5.1% |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B, LoRA r32, 8k | train | 3.760 | 3.530 | 6.1% |
| Qwen3-0.6B, 8k | train / log-prob | 2.571 / 0.703 | 2.421 / 0.644 | 5.8% / 8.5% |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B, 4k | train / log-prob | 5.318 / 1.431 | 4.958 / 1.336 | 6.8% / 6.7% |
| Qwen3-4B, 8k | log-prob | 3.319 | 3.082 | 7.1% |

Std is 0.01–0.2 s; peak memory is identical in every row.

Re-check of the default row against this PR's exact parent (`8e48d72d`), same config, base/PR interleaved, 2 runs × 10 measured batches each, CPU load < 1.3 throughout:

| path | main (s/step) | this PR (s/step) | time saved |
|---|---|---|---|
| train | 1.963 / 1.963 | 1.778 / 1.780 | 9.4% |
| log-prob | 0.564 / 0.567 | 0.517 / 0.517 | 8.5% |

Peak memory 10.63 GB (train) / 8.12 GB (log-prob) in both.

Correctness:
- New `tests/workers/test_fsdp_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs_on_gpu.py`: on a tiny Qwen2 with flash-attn 2, logits and every parameter gradient are **bitwise identical** with and without the kwargs, for both the HF forward and the fused-kernel forward. A negative control (deliberately wrong boundaries) changes the output, so the kwargs do reach the attention.
- New `tests/workers/test_fsdp_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs_on_cpu.py`: the helper's output equals transformers' own `prepare_fa_kwargs_from_position_ids` on the same layouts (including the right-pad segment), plus the gating cases.
- Forward log-probs are bitwise identical between main and this PR on 13 real GSM8K batches; critic values are bitwise equal in eval mode.
- End-to-end SFT, 60 steps × 2 runs each: step-1 loss identical (0.6946185231); the main-vs-PR loss difference (mean 1.9e-4) is within main-vs-main run-to-run noise (2.7e-4, from atomics in the flash-attn / cross-entropy backward kernels).

```
pytest tests/workers/test_fsdp_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs_on_cpu.py tests/workers/test_fsdp_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs_on_gpu.py   # 22 passed
pytest tests/models/test_fsdp_no_padding_on_gpu.py tests/models/test_transformer.py
pre-commit run --files <changed files>   # all hooks passed (ruff, ruff format, mypy, config/docstring/license/naming checks)
```

### API and Usage Example

No API or config change. The optimization is applied automatically when its conditions hold (see below).

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/workers/engine/utils.py`: new `build_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs(cu_seqlens, pad_size)` builds `cu_seq_lens_q/k` and `max_length_q/k` from the packed offsets with one sync per micro-batch. The right-pad added by `pad_packed_inputs` restarts its `position_ids` from 0, so it is one trailing segment, exactly as transformers would infer it.
- `verl/workers/engine/fsdp/transformer_impl.py`: `prepare_model_inputs` adds these kwargs when all of the following hold: the model's `_attn_implementation` is `flash_attention_2` / `flash_attention_3`; it is a text model (no `vision_config` — VLMs go through verl's own mRoPE attention patches); Ulysses SP is off (under SP the boundaries are re-derived from the all-gathered `position_ids`); and the model does not already take `cu_seqlens`. Otherwise the current path is unchanged.
- `verl/models/transformers/dense_common.py`: the fused-kernel forwards now pass extra kwargs through to the base model (previously swallowed as `**loss_kwargs`), so `use_fused_kernels=True` benefits too.

Risks / limitations:
- SP > 1 is gated off and untested here.
- Measured on one consumer GPU with small models; the relative gain shrinks with larger models and micro-batches (~4–7%).
- Not run on NPU, though it uses the same transformers code path as HF's own packing collator.
- A `trust_remote_code` text model whose forward does not accept `**kwargs` would raise `TypeError` (the gate checks only the attention implementation). All in-tree models accept them.

AI assistance: Developed with the help of an AI coding assistant; benchmarks/tests run as described.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the Contribute Guide.
- [x] Apply pre-commit checks.
- [ ] Add / Update the documentation. Not needed: no user-facing API or config change.
- [x] Add unit test(s): `tests/workers/test_fsdp_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs_on_{cpu,gpu}.py`.

- `verl/workers/engine/utils.py`: new `build_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs(cu_seqlens, pad_size)` builds `cu_seq_lens_q/k` and `max_length_q/k` from the packed offsets with one sync per micro-batch. The right-pad added by `pad_packed_inputs` restarts its `position_ids` from 0, so it is one trailing segment, exactly as transformers would infer it.
- `verl/workers/engine/fsdp/transformer_impl.py`: `prepare_model_inputs` adds these kwargs when all of the following hold: the model's `_attn_implementation` is `flash_attention_2` / `flash_attention_3`; it is a text model (no `vision_config` — VLMs go through verl's own mRoPE attention patches); Ulysses SP is off (under SP the boundaries are re-derived from the all-gathered `position_ids`); and the model does not already take `cu_seqlens`. Otherwise the current path is unchanged.
- `verl/models/transformers/dense_common.py`: the fused-kernel forwards now pass extra kwargs through to the base model (previously swallowed as `**loss_kwargs`), so `use_fused_kernels=True` benefits too.

Risks / limitations:
- SP > 1 is gated off and untested here.
- Measured on one consumer GPU with small models; the relative gain shrinks with larger models and micro-batches (~4–7%).
- Not run on NPU, though it uses the same transformers code path as HF's own packing collator.
- A `trust_remote_code` text model whose forward does not accept `**kwargs` would raise `TypeError` (the gate checks only the attention implementation). All in-tree models accept them.

AI assistance: Developed with the help of an AI coding assistant; benchmarks/tests run as described.

- [x] Read the Contribute Guide.
- [x] Apply pre-commit checks.
- [ ] Add / Update the documentation. Not needed: no user-facing API or config change.
- [x] Add unit test(s): `tests/workers/test_fsdp_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs_on_{cpu,gpu}.py`.

+"""Explicit varlen ``FlashAttentionKwargs`` for packed micro-batches in the FSDP engine.
+
+``build_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs`` must describe exactly the segmentation that transformers would
+otherwise re-derive from ``position_ids`` in every attention layer, so these tests compare it with
+``prepare_fa_kwargs_from_position_ids`` on the same packed layout, including the right-pad segment
+appended by ``pad_packed_inputs``.
+
+The ``veomni.*`` imports done by ``transformer_impl`` at module load are stubbed with ``MagicMock``
+as in ``test_packed_pad_to_length_on_cpu.py``.
+"""
+
+import sys
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from transformers.modeling_flash_attention_utils import prepare_fa_kwargs_from_position_ids
+
+for _mod in (
+    "veomni",
+    "veomni.arguments",
+    "veomni.distributed",
+    "veomni.distributed.offloading",
+    "veomni.distributed.torch_parallelize",
+    "veomni.models",
+    "veomni.models.auto",
+    "veomni.optim",
+    "veomni.utils",
+    "veomni.utils.moe_router_replay",
+    "veomni.utils.seqlen_pos_transform_utils",
+    "veomni.models.checkpoint_tensor_loading",
+    "veomni.models.checkpoint_tensor_loading.get_checkpoint_tensor_converter",
+):
+    sys.modules.setdefault(_mod, MagicMock())
+
+from verl.workers.engine.fsdp.transformer_impl import _supports_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs  # noqa: E402
+from verl.workers.engine.utils import build_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs, pad_packed_inputs  # noqa: E402
+
+
+def _packed_position_ids(seqlens: list[int]) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return torch.cat([torch.arange(n) for n in seqlens]).unsqueeze(0)
+
+
+def _cu_seqlens(seqlens: list[int]) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return torch.tensor([0, *seqlens]).cumsum(0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "seqlens, pad_size",
+    [
+        ([5, 3], 0),
+        ([5, 3], 4),
+        ([1, 7, 1, 2], 0),
+        ([1, 7, 1, 2], 9),
+        ([16], 0),
+        ([16], 3),
+    ],
+)
+def test_matches_boundaries_derived_from_position_ids(seqlens, pad_size):
+    input_ids = torch.ones(1, sum(seqlens), dtype=torch.long)
+    _, position_ids = pad_packed_inputs(input_ids, _packed_position_ids(seqlens), pad_size)
+    (ref_cu_q, ref_cu_k), (ref_max_q, ref_max_k) = prepare_fa_kwargs_from_position_ids(position_ids)
+
+    kwargs = build_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs(_cu_seqlens(seqlens), pad_size=pad_size)
+
+    assert kwargs["cu_seq_lens_q"].dtype == torch.int32
+    assert torch.equal(kwargs["cu_seq_lens_q"], ref_cu_q)
+    assert torch.equal(kwargs["cu_seq_lens_k"], ref_cu_k)
+    # Python ints, so neither transformers nor flash-attn needs a device sync to read them.
+    assert type(kwargs["max_length_q"]) is int and type(kwargs["max_length_k"]) is int
+    assert kwargs["max_length_q"] == kwargs["max_length_k"] == int(ref_max_q) == int(ref_max_k)
+
+
+def test_empty_micro_batch_passes_nothing():
+    assert build_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs(torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.long)) == {}
+
+
+def _module(attn_implementation, **config_kwargs):
+    return SimpleNamespace(config=SimpleNamespace(_attn_implementation=attn_implementation, **config_kwargs))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("attn_implementation", ["flash_attention_2", "flash_attention_3"])
+def test_enabled_for_text_models_on_flash_attention(attn_implementation):
+    assert _supports_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs(_module(attn_implementation))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("attn_implementation", ["sdpa", "eager", "flex_attention", None])
+def test_disabled_for_other_attention_implementations(attn_implementation):
+    assert not _supports_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs(_module(attn_implementation))
+
+
+def test_disabled_for_vision_language_models():
+    assert not _supports_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs(_module("flash_attention_2", vision_config=SimpleNamespace()))
+
+
+def test_disabled_without_a_config():
+    assert not _supports_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs(SimpleNamespace())

+"""The FSDP engine passes packed-sequence boundaries to flash attention as explicit varlen kwargs.
+
+Without them transformers re-derives ``cu_seqlens``/``max_seqlen`` from ``position_ids`` in every
+attention layer, which costs several host-device syncs per layer. These tests check that the
+engine emits the kwargs, that they describe the same segmentation as ``position_ids``, and that a
+packed forward/backward with them is bitwise identical to the ``position_ids`` path, both for the
+plain HF forward and for verl's fused-kernel forward.
+"""
+
+import warnings
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from verl.utils.device import get_device_name, is_device_available
+
+if not is_device_available():
+    pytest.skip("Requires an accelerator device", allow_module_level=True)
+
+FLASH_ATTN_VARLEN_KEYS = {"cu_seq_lens_q", "cu_seq_lens_k", "max_length_q", "max_length_k"}
+
+
+def _make_engine(pad_to_length: bool = False, bucket: int = 16, pass_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs: bool = True):
+    with warnings.catch_warnings():
+        warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=UserWarning)
+        from verl.workers.engine.fsdp.transformer_impl import FSDPEngineWithLMHead
+
+    engine = FSDPEngineWithLMHead.__new__(FSDPEngineWithLMHead)
+    engine.pad_to_length = pad_to_length
+    engine.pad_to_length_bucket = bucket
+    engine.use_ulysses_sp = False
+    if pass_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs:
+        engine.pass_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs = True
+    return engine
+
+
+def _make_micro_batch(seqlens: list[int], device: str):
+    from tensordict import TensorDict
+
+    from verl.utils import tensordict_utils as tu
+    from verl.utils.dataset.dataset_utils import DatasetPadMode
+
+    def nested(rows):
+        return torch.nested.as_nested_tensor(rows, layout=torch.jagged)
+
+    micro_batch = TensorDict(
+        {
+            "input_ids": nested([torch.arange(1, n + 1, device=device) for n in seqlens]),
+            "position_ids": nested([torch.arange(n, device=device) for n in seqlens]),
+            "temperature": torch.ones(len(seqlens), device=device),
+        },
+        batch_size=[len(seqlens)],
+    )
+    tu.assign_non_tensor(
+        micro_batch, use_remove_padding=True, use_fused_kernels=False, pad_mode=DatasetPadMode.NO_PADDING
+    )
+    return micro_batch
+
+
+def test_prepare_model_inputs_passes_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs():
+    from transformers.modeling_flash_attention_utils import prepare_fa_kwargs_from_position_ids
+
+    device = get_device_name()
+    model_inputs, output_args = _make_engine().prepare_model_inputs(_make_micro_batch([5, 3], device))
+
+    expected = torch.tensor([0, 5, 8], device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(model_inputs["cu_seq_lens_q"], expected)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(model_inputs["cu_seq_lens_k"], expected)
+    assert model_inputs["max_length_q"] == model_inputs["max_length_k"] == 5
+    assert output_args["pad_size"] == 0
+    # The same boundaries transformers would re-derive from position_ids in every attention layer.
+    (cu_seqlens_from_position_ids, _), _ = prepare_fa_kwargs_from_position_ids(model_inputs["position_ids"])
+    torch.testing.assert_close(model_inputs["cu_seq_lens_q"], cu_seqlens_from_position_ids)
+
+
+def test_prepare_model_inputs_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs_cover_the_static_pad():
+    from transformers.modeling_flash_attention_utils import prepare_fa_kwargs_from_position_ids
+
+    device = get_device_name()
+    engine = _make_engine(pad_to_length=True, bucket=16)
+    model_inputs, output_args = engine.prepare_model_inputs(_make_micro_batch([5, 3], device))
+
+    assert output_args["pad_size"] == 8
+    assert model_inputs["input_ids"].shape == (1, 16)
+    (cu_seqlens_from_position_ids, _), (max_length, _) = prepare_fa_kwargs_from_position_ids(
+        model_inputs["position_ids"]
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(model_inputs["cu_seq_lens_q"], cu_seqlens_from_position_ids)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        model_inputs["cu_seq_lens_q"], torch.tensor([0, 5, 8, 16], device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+    )
+    assert model_inputs["max_length_q"] == int(max_length) == 8
+
+
+def test_prepare_model_inputs_skips_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs_when_unsupported():
+    engine = _make_engine(pass_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs=False)
+    model_inputs, _ = engine.prepare_model_inputs(_make_micro_batch([5, 3], get_device_name()))
+
+    assert not FLASH_ATTN_VARLEN_KEYS & model_inputs.keys()
+
+
+def _tiny_qwen2(device: str, use_fused_kernels: bool = False):
+    from transformers import Qwen2Config, Qwen2ForCausalLM
+
+    from verl.models.transformers.monkey_patch import apply_monkey_patch
+
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    config = Qwen2Config(
+        vocab_size=128,
+        hidden_size=64,
+        intermediate_size=128,
+        num_hidden_layers=2,
+        num_attention_heads=4,
+        num_key_value_heads=2,
+        attn_implementation="flash_attention_2",
+    )
+    model = Qwen2ForCausalLM(config).to(device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    apply_monkey_patch(
+        model=model,
+        use_remove_padding=True,
+        use_fused_kernels=use_fused_kernels,
+        fused_kernels_backend="torch" if use_fused_kernels else None,
+    )
+    return model
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("seqlens", [[37, 5, 64, 1, 20], [48]])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_fused_kernels", [False, True], ids=["hf_forward", "fused_forward"])
+def test_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs_match_position_ids_path(seqlens, use_fused_kernels, monkeypatch):
+    """A packed forward/backward with the explicit kwargs is bitwise identical to the one where the
+    boundaries are re-derived from position_ids in every layer."""
+    pytest.importorskip("flash_attn")
+    from verl.workers.engine.utils import build_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs
+
+    # flash-attn's backward accumulates dQ with atomics unless it runs in deterministic mode.
+    monkeypatch.setenv("FLASH_ATTENTION_DETERMINISTIC", "1")
+    device = get_device_name()
+    model = _tiny_qwen2(device, use_fused_kernels=use_fused_kernels)
+    vocab_size = model.config.vocab_size
+
+    input_ids = torch.randint(0, vocab_size, (1, sum(seqlens)), device=device)
+    position_ids = torch.cat([torch.arange(n, device=device) for n in seqlens]).unsqueeze(0)
+    cu_seqlens = torch.tensor([0, *seqlens], device=device).cumsum(0)
+
+    def run(**kwargs):
+        model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
+        if use_fused_kernels:
+            out = model(input_ids=input_ids, position_ids=position_ids, use_cache=False, return_dict=True, **kwargs)
+            result = out.log_probs
+        else:
+            result = model(input_ids=input_ids, position_ids=position_ids, use_cache=False, **kwargs).logits
+        result.float().square().mean().backward()
+        return result.detach(), {name: p.grad.clone() for name, p in model.named_parameters()}
+
+    ref_out, ref_grads = run()
+    out, grads = run(**build_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs(cu_seqlens))
+
+    assert torch.equal(out, ref_out)
+    for name, grad in grads.items():
+        assert torch.equal(grad, ref_grads[name]), name
+
+    # The kwargs do reach the attention layers: merging all sequences into one changes the result.
+    merged = build_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs(torch.tensor([0, sum(seqlens)], device=device))
+    if len(seqlens) > 1:
+        assert not torch.equal(run(**merged)[0], ref_out)

+def build_flash_attn_varlen_kwargs(cu_seqlens: torch.Tensor, pad_size: int = 0) -> dict:
+    """Varlen ``FlashAttentionKwargs`` for a packed ``(1, total_nnz)`` micro-batch.
+
+    The packed boundaries are already known from the nested-tensor offsets. Without these kwargs,
+    transformers re-derives them from ``position_ids`` inside every attention layer and flash-attn
+    converts the tensor ``max_seqlen`` to an int, which forces several host-device syncs per layer
+    (again in the activation-checkpoint recompute and in the backward). Here they cost one sync per
+    micro-batch, and the attention inputs stay identical.
+
+    Args:

+        pad_size: right-padding appended by :func:`pad_packed_inputs`. Its ``position_ids`` restart

+        ``max_length_q``/``max_length_k`` (python ints), or an empty dict for an empty micro-batch.
